reference: GNU Git (git hash-object, cat-file, mktree, ls-tree, and commit-tree) runs only in the reference fixture. Its object IDs and readers are the independent oracle; no expected operation output is derived from bash-os. Contract metadata is based on Bash's type/help builtins and obj_doc/short_doc in the pinned source. Parity cases require git.
coverage: Bash type and short-help metadata for the obj builtin.
Git-compatible SHA-1 object IDs for empty and binary blob data.
hash --stdin-paths with multiple paths and repeated direct invocation in one shell.
Loose blob creation, cat/type/size reads, and upward repository discovery.
Batch and batch-check protocols with full IDs, abbreviated IDs, missing IDs, and repeated stdin reads.
Tree creation and NUL-safe parse-tree output compared with git mktree and git ls-tree, including a spaced filename.
Deterministic parent and child commit creation, with parse-commit checked against git cat-file.
Packed blob read/type/size/batch-check from an independently generated and verified Git pack/index with no loose fallback.
exclusions: This suite does not cover worktrees, alternates, hash filters, annotated tags, malformed object stores, or NUL-truncated variable binding.
All runnable writes stay within each runner-created private private fixture; no host or privileged operation is used.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports obj as a builtin, using Bash's documented type -t contract.
Confirm help -s exposes the builtin's documented short synopsis from obj_struct.short_doc.
Compare the empty-blob object ID with GNU Git; this checks the object header, SHA-1, and empty-input boundary.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '' | obj hash --stdin
else
  printf '' | git hash-object --stdin
fi

cases.purpose: Check two path inputs, a filename containing a space, and a second direct stdin-paths invocation in the same shell.

printf 'second file\n' > 'with space'
printf 'first\nwith space\n' > paths
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  obj hash --stdin-paths < paths
  obj hash --stdin-paths < paths

  git hash-object --stdin-paths < paths

cases.purpose: Compare loose blob write, type, size, and raw cat bytes with GNU Git; the final read runs below the repository root to exercise upward discovery. The filesystem snapshot is excluded because GNU Git and obj write different valid zlib streams for identical loose-object payloads; IDs, type, size, and raw cat bytes remain compared. Every retained compressed object is independently inflated with Python zlib; its SHA-1, header, size and full payload are compared. Compressed byte streams inherently vary, so compare_tree is false; raw files remain in validation evidence.
cases.script:
mkdir -p repo/.git/objects/info repo/.git/refs/heads
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > repo/.git/HEAD
printf '[core]\n\tbare = false\n' > repo/.git/config
printf 'blob bytes\000with NUL\n' > repo/payload
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  oid=$(obj blob repo/payload -r repo)
  printf '%s\n' "$oid"
  obj type "$oid" -r repo
  obj size "$oid" -r repo
  mkdir -p repo/nested
  cd repo/nested
  obj cat "$oid"
else
  oid=$(git -C repo hash-object -w payload)
  printf '%s\n' "$oid"
  git -C repo cat-file -t "$oid"
  git -C repo cat-file -s "$oid"
  mkdir -p repo/nested
  cd repo/nested
  git cat-file blob "$oid"
fi
cd ../..
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'CHECK'
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, zlib
for p in sorted(Path('repo/.git/objects').glob('*/*')):
    if not p.is_file() or len(p.parent.name)!=2: continue
    raw=zlib.decompress(p.read_bytes())
    oid=p.parent.name+p.name
    assert hashlib.sha1(raw).hexdigest()==oid, (str(p),raw)
    head,body=raw.split(b'\0',1)
    kind,size=head.split(b' ',1)
    assert int(size)==len(body)
    print('independent-object',oid,kind.decode(),len(body),raw.hex())
CHECK

cases.purpose: Compare obj tree and parse-tree -z with Git mktree/ls-tree. The NUL record keeps the spaced filename unambiguous. The filesystem snapshot is excluded because GNU Git and obj write different valid zlib streams for identical loose-object payloads; tree IDs and NUL-delimited parse output remain byte-compared. Every retained compressed object is independently inflated with Python zlib; its SHA-1, header, size and full payload are compared. Compressed byte streams inherently vary, so compare_tree is false; raw files remain in validation evidence.
cases.script:
mkdir -p repo/.git/objects/info repo/.git/refs/heads
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > repo/.git/HEAD
printf '[core]\n\tbare = false\n' > repo/.git/config
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  blob=$(printf 'tree child\n' | obj hash --stdin -w -r repo)
  tree=$(printf '100644 path with space.txt %s\n' "$blob" | obj tree -r repo)
  printf '%s\n' "$tree"
  obj parse-tree "$tree" -r repo -z
else
  blob=$(printf 'tree child\n' | git -C repo hash-object --stdin -w)
  tree=$(printf '100644 blob %s\tpath with space.txt\n' "$blob" | git -C repo mktree)
  printf '%s\n' "$tree"
  git -C repo ls-tree -z "$tree" |
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
      meta=${entry%%$'\t'*}
      name=${entry#*$'\t'}
      read -r mode type oid <<< "$meta"
      printf '%s %s\t%s\000' "$mode" "$oid" "$name"
    done
fi
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'CHECK'
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, zlib
for p in sorted(Path('repo/.git/objects').glob('*/*')):
    if not p.is_file() or len(p.parent.name)!=2: continue
    raw=zlib.decompress(p.read_bytes())
    oid=p.parent.name+p.name
    assert hashlib.sha1(raw).hexdigest()==oid, (str(p),raw)
    head,body=raw.split(b'\0',1)
    kind,size=head.split(b' ',1)
    assert int(size)==len(body)
    print('independent-object',oid,kind.decode(),len(body),raw.hex())
CHECK

cases.purpose: Create a deterministic two-commit chain and compare parse-commit output with Git's raw commit body, including its parent, identities, timestamps, and message. The filesystem snapshot is excluded because GNU Git and obj write different valid zlib streams for identical loose-object payloads; commit parse output and status remain compared. Every retained compressed object is independently inflated with Python zlib; its SHA-1, header, size and full payload are compared. Compressed byte streams inherently vary, so compare_tree is false; raw files remain in validation evidence.
cases.script:
: > empty-input
mkdir -p repo/.git/objects/info repo/.git/refs/heads
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > repo/.git/HEAD
printf '[core]\n\tbare = false\n' > repo/.git/config
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  tree=$(obj tree -r repo <empty-input)
  root=$(obj commit -t "$tree" -m root -a 'Fixture Author <author@fixture.invalid>' -c 'Fixture Committer <committer@fixture.invalid>' -d 1750000000 -r repo)
  child=$(obj commit -t "$tree" -p "$root" -m child -a 'Fixture Author <author@fixture.invalid>' -c 'Fixture Committer <committer@fixture.invalid>' -d 1750000100 -r repo)
  obj parse-commit "$child" -r repo
else
  tree=$(git -C repo mktree <empty-input)
  root=$(GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Fixture Author' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='author@fixture.invalid' GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000000 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Fixture Committer' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='committer@fixture.invalid' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000000 +0000' git -C repo commit-tree "$tree" -m root)
  child=$(GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='Fixture Author' GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL='author@fixture.invalid' GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='1750000100 +0000' GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Fixture Committer' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='committer@fixture.invalid' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='1750000100 +0000' git -C repo commit-tree "$tree" -p "$root" -m child)
  git -C repo cat-file commit "$child"
fi
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'CHECK'
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, zlib
for p in sorted(Path('repo/.git/objects').glob('*/*')):
    if not p.is_file() or len(p.parent.name)!=2: continue
    raw=zlib.decompress(p.read_bytes())
    oid=p.parent.name+p.name
    assert hashlib.sha1(raw).hexdigest()==oid, (str(p),raw)
    head,body=raw.split(b'\0',1)
    kind,size=head.split(b' ',1)
    assert int(size)==len(body)
    print('independent-object',oid,kind.decode(),len(body),raw.hex())
CHECK

cases.purpose: Check the documented Git-compatible fatal status for a missing object; wording is allowed to differ while stderr must be present.
cases.script:
mkdir -p repo/.git/objects/info repo/.git/refs/heads
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > repo/.git/HEAD
printf '[core]\n\tbare = false\n' > repo/.git/config
missing=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  obj cat "$missing" -r repo
else

cases.purpose: Read a tiny pack/index independently produced and verified by Git after deleting its loose copy; compare type, size, payload and batch-check. All artifacts stay in the private relative repository.
cases.script:
mkdir -p repo/.git/objects/info repo/.git/objects/pack repo/.git/refs/heads
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > repo/.git/HEAD
printf '[core]\n\tbare = false\n' > repo/.git/config
oid=$(printf 'independent packed blob\n' | /usr/bin/git -C repo hash-object --stdin -w)
pack=$(printf '%s\n' "$oid" | /usr/bin/git -C repo pack-objects .git/objects/pack/fixture)
/usr/bin/git -C repo verify-pack ".git/objects/pack/fixture-$pack.idx"
/usr/bin/python3 - "$oid" <<'CHECK'
from pathlib import Path
import sys
oid=sys.argv[1]
Path('repo/.git/objects',oid[:2],oid[2:]).unlink()
CHECK
if [[ $(type -t obj) == builtin ]]; then
  obj type "$oid" -r repo
  obj size "$oid" -r repo
  obj cat "$oid" -r repo
  printf '%s\n' "$oid" | obj --batch-check -r repo
else
  git -C repo cat-file -t "$oid"
  git -C repo cat-file -s "$oid"
  git -C repo cat-file blob "$oid"
  printf '%s\n' "$oid" | git -C repo cat-file --batch-check
fi
